properties.description:
TWO BREAKING CHANGES TAKEN ON PURPOSE, both DECLINED hours earlier on the ground that they would break consumers. `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` (Anthony, 2026-08-17) reversed that ground: before a stability commitment exists the price of a break is at its lowest and rises with every user, so "it would break consumers" argues for doing it NOW. (The guard matched `dec:a-misnaming-is-fixed-in-the-message-not-the-key`, which is the DECISION that first declined this and now records its own reversal; this is the built thing that carries it out. Also distinct from `cap:a-finding-describes-the-walk-that-produced-it`, which fixed the MESSAGE and left both of these standing.)

(1) `disconnected_community` IS NOW `unthreaded_cluster`. The old key asserted unreachability while the detector computed something narrower — connected components over `design_network()`, which drops nine node types and every review record and does not count CONTAINS, covering 1133 of a 2413-node graph. `unthreaded` names what is actually missing, a traceability edge, and cannot be misread as "unreachable in the graph". The ility source string moves with it.

⭐ THE COST THAT DECIDED AGAINST IT WAS NEVER MEASURED, and measuring it is what made the call obvious: the key appears in 14 source/test files, 6 live docs and 41 prose mentions in the export, and is PERSISTED AS DATA NOWHERE — no node property holds it as a value. No observation, acknowledgement or ility reading needed migrating. A rename feared as a migration was a sed and a doc pass.

(2) UNSCOPED `detect_defects` RETURNS `{swept, defects}` INSTEAD OF A BARE LIST. `swept.nodes` is what it examined, `swept.rules` names the checks that ran, `swept.design_network_nodes` reports the narrower topology walk rather than hiding it, and `swept.note` appears ONLY when the sweep could not have found anything. An empty result now says which empty it is — exercised and found nothing, or nothing to examine — instead of leaving a zero to be read as permission before `apply_heal`, which deletes nodes. The scoped sibling has answered this way since 2026-08-09, so one tool was answering one question two ways and the honest half was the one fewer people call. `open_defects()` is the bare list for engine-internal callers.

WHAT IT COST, recorded as evidence for the rule rather than for the change: five real consumers of the old shape broke and were FIXED rather than shimmed — `smoke_mcp.py` in three places, `model_the_loop.py`, `build_design_graph.py`, and `bl124_instrument.py`, which now reads both shapes deliberately because it is an instrument that may be pointed at an older server. 53 test call sites moved to `open_defects()`. One toolsnap golden moved.

⚠️ AND A FALSE CLAIM WAS CAUGHT IN THE WRITING. The first draft of `HealCategory::ALL`'s doc comment said the compiler enforced that every variant is listed. It does not — `as_str`'s exhaustive match forces an author into the impl block, but nothing makes them extend the list, and a missing entry would make `swept.rules` UNDERSTATE the sweep. The comment now says it is hand-maintained and names the test that actually holds it. Shipping an unchecked claim about a check, inside the change whose subject is reports that overstate, would have been the joke writing itself.
properties.name: A defect sweep returns what it examined, and the category names what it computes
